title: Jill's Dairy (Chas McIvor)
style: Afro-folk fingerpicked acoustic guitar warm alto female vocal storytelling 96bpm brushed snare Zimbabwe dairy farm portrait quiet certainty character portrait unhurried dawn
lyrics:
[Intro - soft fingerpicked guitar, dawn feeling]
Before the farm wakes
Before the light decides what colour it is
Jill is already there

[Verse 1]
Four in the morning, the dairy doesn't wait
The cows know the schedule better than any clock
She moved through them easy, she knew every name
Didn't need to think about what comes next
The rhythm was hers, the morning was hers
Quiet in the way that real things are quiet
Not because nothing is happening
But because everything is

[Verse 2]
People talk about the hard life
As though it needs explaining to the ones who lived it
Jill just nodded and went back to work
The kind of woman who doesn't need convincing
You knew where you stood with Jill
Which was on solid ground
She didn't say it twice
She didn't need to

[Chorus]
Jill's dairy
In the hours before the world wakes
Jill's dairy
Where the real work gets done in the dark
Jill's dairy
Where certainty is a morning habit
And the cows come home
And the cows come home
Because Jill is there

[Bridge - spoken, gentle]
Some people hold families together loudly.
Jill did it quietly.
Which is harder.
The dairy didn't fail.
The family didn't fail.
These things are connected.

[Outro - guitar fading, unhurried]
Jill's dairy
In everything Kerri does without making a fuss
Jill's dairy
In how the morning gets handled without drama
Jill's dairy
Still running somewhere
In the family it made
